metadata.name: ABCD2 Score for TIA
metadata.summary: 7-point score estimating 2-, 7-, and 90-day stroke risk after transient ischemic attack.
clinical_pearls: Low ABCD2 (0–3) does NOT exclude high-risk etiologies such as symptomatic carotid stenosis, atrial fibrillation, or crescendo TIA.
Higher ABCD2 scores generally correlate with increased short-term stroke risk and higher likelihood of true TIA (Josephson et al., 2008).
Patients with low baseline stroke risk (≤ 2%) and low ABCD2 score (0–2) have a low 7-day stroke risk (0.4–0.8%).
Pitfall — Emergency department performance: Large prospective ED validation (Perry et al., 2011) showed poor sensitivity for identifying low-risk patients and poor specificity for high-risk patients.
Pitfall — Setting & rater bias: ABCD2 was derived in outpatient cohorts and shows lower accuracy when applied by non-specialists or in low-baseline-risk populations.

options.label: Other symptoms (e.g., isolated sensory loss, visual symptoms, ataxia)
Unilateral weakness (with or without speech disturbance)

interpretation.label: Low 2-Day Stroke Risk (~1.0%)
interpretation.summary: ABCD2 0–3: lower early risk, but urgent vessel/cardiac workup is still required.

interpretation.label: Moderate 2-Day Stroke Risk (~4.1%)
interpretation.summary: ABCD2 4–5: moderate early stroke risk; urgent evaluation and secondary prevention indicated.

interpretation.label: High 2-Day Stroke Risk (~8.1%)
interpretation.summary: ABCD2 6–7: high early stroke risk; immediate inpatient/rapid-access TIA workup.

assessment_guides.title: Clinical Features Hierarchy
bedside_steps: Score the highest-weighting feature present during the TIA episode.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: If BOTH unilateral weakness and speech disturbance occurred, score 2 (not 3).
Negative DWI-MRI does not rule out TIA; positive DWI-MRI indicates acute ischemic stroke.

references.citation: Johnston SC, Rothwell PM, Nguyen-Huynh MN, et al. Validation and refinement of scores to predict very early stroke risk after transient ischaemic attack. Lancet. 2007;369(9558):283-292.
